You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Claude Code: `references/claude-code-tools.md`
- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`
- Muse: `references/muse-tools.md`

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

- claim-checking: Checks claims pasted from other AI tools against primary sources and wants the verdicts saved in files, not accepted as stated.
- scope-narrowing: Cuts specific sub-areas from a research brief and expects Claude to honor the cut without reopening it.
- thoroughness: Asks for every item to be checked in full, not a sample (e.g. 'check and read all the groups, not just group 7') and expects the specific issues raised to be addressed.
- release-scope: When asked to merge and release, expects the homepage, help pages, guides and changelog to be updated in the same pass.
- feature-defaults: Wants new features always on by default with a simple switch to turn them off, rather than opt-in slash commands.
- completion-check: Asks directly whether commits and syncs are finished before accepting work as done, and expects a verified answer.

# Global notes (all projects)

## MOAA setup (this machine)

- **Canonical source:** `~/code/claude-kit`, the public GitHub repo [ahmadhammoud56/MOAA](https://github.com/ahmadhammoud56/MOAA), currently at v0.19.0 on branch `release/0.19.0` (council 1.7.0, arena 0.7.0, War Room 0.7.1, allies 0.3.0, strata 0.6.0, moaa-catalog 0.4.4, prompt-refiner 0.1.2, team 0.1.0, moaa-core 0.2.0, prismantis 0.34.0 with the PNG button on via `PRISMANTIS_PNG_BUTTON`). Edit there and nowhere else.
- **Context mode: all-on.** Every catalog plugin is enabled (claude-mem and prismantis stay off) and the skill listing is trimmed in `settings.json` (`skillListingMaxDescChars` 200, `skillListingBudgetFraction` 0.003). `moaa-catalog`'s prompt hook names matching skills, including enabled ones whose descriptions are trimmed. Switch with `py scripts/install.py --mode all-on|lean`; `--report` shows the listing cost, `/context` the exact figure.
- **Always on:** prompt-refiner turns each new request into a brief (asks about ambiguous points with options, saves `.briefs/`, gives subagents the brief); off with `py "<plugin dir>/refiner.py" off`, one prompt with a `raw:` prefix. strata's context handoff writes `.claude/handoff/<stamp>/HANDOFF.md` + `CONTEXT.md` at ~85% context and the next chat resumes; `strata.py handoff off|threshold N|mode compact|recall off`. strata's virtual context recalls evicted turns (tool results included) after handoffs and compactions; its project RAG (`rag.py search|status|off`) adds matching file passages with `path:lines`. strata's canary asks for an invisible `[//]: # (strata:ok)` line at the end of each reply; two long replies without it above 30% context start the handoff early (`strata.py canary off|misses N|floor N`). Second-brain vault: `strata.py vault init` (default `~/code/brain`, local git, never auto-committed), `strata.py capture "TEXT"`, daily line per chat, `/strata:wiki distill` weekly; `vault off`. moaa-core's guard notes long inline `python -c` (`MOAA_GUARD=off`); `/moaa-core:project-docs` audits AGENTS.md/ARCHITECTURE/PRD etc.
- **Team board:** `team` plugin (`team.py init|join|board|claim|update|handoff|send|inbox|note`) lets people on separate Claude accounts share one repo via a `team-board` branch; never share credentials or usage between accounts.
- **Long tasks:** `/specialist-council:long-task` keeps `brief.md` (acceptance checks), `progress.md`, `checks.md` (claim-table evidence review) and `resume.md` in `.claude/long-task/<slug>/`, and gives a `/goal` line. Use it for multi-session work instead of ad-hoc handoff notes.
- **Knowledge and loops:** `/strata:wiki` (Karpathy LLM Wiki: Claude compiles sources into linked pages; `graph.py lint`), `/strata:graph` (typed claim-source findings; `graph.py check` grounding score), `/agent-arena-mode:karpathy-loop` (fixed metric, keep/discard). `claude-code-setup` recommends automations per project.
- **Updates:** this machine is a clone (directory source): update with `py scripts/install.py --update`; moaa-catalog announces new releases at session start (daily check).
- **Secrets:** the installer's deny rules block the Read tool on `.env*` files, `keys.env`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws/credentials` and `*.pem`. Check MCP servers with `py scripts/install.py --status --mcp`.
- **Agent tools:** the 60 council role agents carry an explicit core `tools:` list (no Agent, no MCP tools). Forged members keep every tool except Agent (`disallowedTools: [Agent]`, MCP included).
- **Allies and Strata (0.7.0):** `allies` hands tasks to Codex, Gemini and OpenCode (v1 `opencode-ai@1`, installed; free zero-retention Zen models only unless `MOAA_ALLIES_MODELS` names another; no login needed) (ready here; Kimi and DeepSeek are blocked on the campus network) and to a local OmniRoute gateway (`allies.py omniroute start`; no providers connected yet). Keys live only in `~/.claude/allies/keys.env`, never in a repo. `strata` is the layered memory and replaces claude-mem, which is disabled.
- **Health checks:** `py scripts/install.py --status` compares the install with the repo (changes nothing); `py scripts/install.py --doctor` runs every pre-commit check.
- **Marketplace:** `moaa` is a directory source pointing at that folder.
- **Install scope:** all plugins, skills, agents and MCP servers (`rea`, `ansys`) are installed at user scope, so they work in every project.
- **Specialist Council:**
  - Installed as the `specialist-council@moaa` plugin; its agents are named `specialist-council:council-<role>`.
  - Each role's model and effort are in the plugin's `profile.json` and the agent frontmatter; see `MODELS.md` in the repo.
  - Resolve a role's settings with `python "<plugin dir>/council.py" resolve --role ROLE [--style S]`, run as a single standalone command. Forged members use `--role forged-<slug>`.
- **Agent Arena:**
  - Installed as `agent-arena-mode@moaa`. Its library is `~/.claude/plugins/data/agent-arena-mode-moaa/library.sqlite3`; `library.py` finds it automatically when run by hand.
  - Forged council members live in `~/.claude/specialist-council/forged/` and `~/.claude/agents/council-forged-*.md`.
- **Before reinstalling or changing a marketplace:** uninstalling a plugin deletes its data folder. Back up the arena `library.sqlite3` first.
- **Release routine for repo changes:** bump the plugin version, run `python scripts/install.py` (it updates the marketplace), run `python scripts/install.py --doctor` and, for any changed hook, the live suites in `python scripts/e2e.py` (`--list` shows cost), then commit and push. Tag or announce the release only after the macOS and Linux CI runs pass. Keep `LICENSE` as plain MIT text so GitHub keeps detecting it.

## Open to-dos (the user's own; mention when relevant, don't act unasked)

1. **claude-mem can't save memories.** Its provider allowance has been used up since 2026-10-07. Switch the provider in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` or wait for the reset. Never restart the worker.
2. **Claude CLI: update to 2.1.304 or newer when winget offers it** (`winget upgrade --id Anthropic.ClaudeCode`). It fixes the whole skill list being resent on plugin reloads. Winget manages the CLI again (2.1.302 since 2026-10-22); don't use `claude update`, which swaps the binary outside winget.
3. **After updating any third-party plugin,** run `python scripts/sync_catalog.py` in `~/code/claude-kit` and push. That re-pins the catalog and regenerates the README plugin list. After changing a model or effort preset, also run `python scripts/models_doc.py`. To update vendored skills, run `python scripts/sync_skills.py` (`--check` first).

## Working rules (added by the self-improve loop)

- Read a file before editing or overwriting it; never Edit or Write a file you have not read in this session. After a context continuation or compaction, re-read the file first: earlier reads no longer count.
- On Windows, give Bash commands as literal single commands. Avoid `${}`, variables, `~` in assignments and `&&`/`;` chains unless needed; split into separate calls so the permission checker can approve them.
- If `python` exits 49 ("Python was not found"), the Microsoft Store alias is shadowing it: use `py` or the full interpreter path.
- For Python longer than one line, write a `.py` file in the scratchpad and run it, instead of inline `python -c` in Bash or PowerShell (quoting breaks there).
